industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying the view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): technology saw $5.5 billion of net selling in the week, the most since January 2025 (Jefferies, 17 Oct), the rotation came out of it, and Wood says 'the easy money in semis is made'; against that, Jefferies finds sector pockets still upgrading inside it (analogue chips, optical networking, artificial-intelligence memory) and Morgan Stanley still rates North American semiconductors Attractive. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, B prior at industry level, carried by Semiconductors at A. The industry row stays C because the industry is split: Semiconductors (D), Software B2B Enterprise (D), Fintech (D) and Games (D) carry the Underweight; IT services, Hardware and vertical software stay Neutral. Counter-case for D: the heaviest net selling in 21 months is a regime statement; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Underweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the discount-rate case holds (the Fed hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%) and no source spoke to software this week. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, C prior, the disagreement stated: a rank rising from a floor. Six Pool names, Sinch at Sell-side Momentum A the counter. Back to F if relative strength falls to D with the discount rate still rising, to C if the Fed path is marked down.

geography.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence for a view named and judged thin. Goldman (19 Oct) names the UK index among those rallying with non-AI, low-beta exposures; its UK Weekly Kickstart 'The Value of Earnings' and the podcast 'The cavalry isn't coming: UK stocks' were titles only; the Bank of England and gilt yields were not read. One clause of index leadership on a 191-stock row, the largest in the table, is not a country view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to B if a second source makes the UK case with a rate path read.
